Quiz yourself and grade assignments against rubrics as a student
A student uses Claude for adaptive self-quizzing from lecture materials, rubric-based grading of assignments to find gaps, and per-class context kept in Projects.
·
Sep 1, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The student used Claude’s web app in three repeatable ways. For studying, they pasted lecture slides or chapter text and had Claude ask one question at a time, only revealing answers after an attempt and increasing difficulty when they were getting things right. For assignments, they pasted the rubric, prompt, and draft so Claude could point out where points would be lost; they also kept a separate Claude Project for each class, loaded with the syllabus, slides, and past assignments.
How it went
The post says this beat rereading notes, was better at finding gaps than writing the assignment itself, and made class questions more specific because Claude had real course context. It falls short on exact prompting details for how the questioning gets harder.
Worth knowing
The clearest practical catch is that this depends on keeping each class’s materials organized in Claude Projects and supplying complete rubrics and course documents yourself.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I'm studying [course name]. I'll paste my lecture notes below. Quiz me one question at a time, adjusting difficulty based on my answers, and after each answer tell me what I got right and wrong. After 15 questions, list the topics I'm weakest on and suggest what to review. Then I'll paste an assignment and its rubric, and you should grade my draft against the rubric and point out gaps. Notes: [paste notes]
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeWorkflows/comments/1vtsh8t/workflow_student_workflows_adaptive_selfquizzing
